newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court denies export refunds on lost grain bound for Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Court denies export refunds on lost grain bound for Vietnam.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday a European grain exporter whose ship sank outside Community waters had no right to export refunds on the lost grain.
The court's reasoning revolved around whether a non-variable rate of refund had been fixed for the country receiving the grain, in this instance, Vietnam.

"The rules on entitlement to variable refunds stemmed from a concern to prevent abuse," the court said. "This risk of abuse exists not only where different rates have been fixed for various countries, but also where no rate has been fixed for one country."

The Greek insurance company, Astir AE, covered a grain trader's losses after his ship sank outside Community waters, believing it was entitled under insurance rules of subrogation to the trader's right to an export refund. The Greek government denied its claim for 7,351,674 drachmas.
The Commission regulation in question provides payment of a refund in the event of a force majeure event, if a non-variable refund has been established.
But the court said export refunds after a force majeure event are granted "only if the product has been imported into a non-member country for which the refund is prescribed."
The court did not accept Astir's argument that there "is no variation of the rate of refund according to destination, but rather a derogation from the right to a refund for certain destinations."
"Export refunds for agricultural products - Loss of goods in transit by reason of force majeure - Variable refund"
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Greek)
Reference fromt eh Polimeles Protodikio, Athens, for a preliminary ruling in the case between

on the interpretation of articles 10(4), 20 and 21 of Commission regulation (EEC) No 2730/79 of 29 November 1979 laying down common detailed rules for the application of the system of export refunds on agricultural products (OJ 1979 L 317, p. 1)

Articles 10(4), 20 and 21 of Commission regulation (EEC) No 2730/79 of 29 November 1979 laying down common detailed rules for the application of the system of export refunds on agricultural products must be interpreted as meaning that a trader is not entitled to an export refund where the product concerned has perished in transit as a result of force majeure, after leaving the geographical teritory of the Community, and where the same rate of refund has been fixed for all non-member countries, with the exception of one single country, for which no refund has been found.
